These rows were in the draft table and contradicted wording that is already shipped (or fixed in the house table). They are removed so that ratification does not freeze the wrong word; the units follow the shipped wording.

| ἀπηνής | "harsh" | shipped 18.381: "unkind" in both layers; "harsh" reserved for χαλεπός |
| τηλεδαπός | "from distant lands" | shipped 14.415 "from a far-off land" (`i`), "from-a-far-land" (`l`), odyssey-029 "from far-off lands"; "distant" is listed there as avoided. The units now say "from far-off lands" |
| κακότης | "misfortune" | published parts render κακότης "misery" (odyssey-034, 064, 085, 087, and 010 in `l`) |
| ἐξαίτους ἑκατόμβας | "choice hecatombs" in both layers | odyssey-023 (unit at line 101) already ships the same two words: `l` "picked-out hecatombs", `i` "choice hecatombs"; the units now follow it |

**Flag for the owner (not changed here):** the shipped table row λέβης (15.84) says "cauldron" and lists "basin" as avoided, but published odyssey-002 (unit at line 136, "a silver basin") and odyssey-013 (unit at line 440, "a basin worked with flowers") already render λέβης "basin". The units follow the table row, as instructed; one of the two should be brought into line before the poem is complete.

**Left in the table, flagged:** ἀτιτάλλω "fostered" (19.354) is a new word for a verb the published parts render "rear" (odyssey-053, 091) or "raise" (066); it was chosen to keep it apart from τρέφω "reared" in the same clause, and is not contradicted by any table row. The owner may prefer "brought up" or "reared" for one of the two.
